tasks.title: Setup Project Foundation
tasks.description: Initialize the project structure, install all dependencies, and configure build scripts and core configuration files within the existing Git repository.
tasks.details:
1. Create `package.json` to manage dependencies: `npm init -y`
2. Install all dev dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm install -D eleventy @11ty/eleventy-plugin-rss @11ty/eleventy-plugin-syntaxhighlight luxon tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer npm-run-all @tailwindcss/typography
   ```
3. Create the full project directory structure as defined in section 5.2 of the PRD.
4. Initialize Tailwind (`npx tailwindcss init -p`), which creates `tailwind.config.js` and `postcss.config.js`.
5. Create initial placeholder files: `.eleventy.js` and `netlify.toml`.
6. Update `package.json` with the scripts from section 5.3 of the PRD.
7. Create a `.gitignore` file for `node_modules/` and `_site/`.

tasks.title: Configure Eleventy, Tailwind, and Site Data
tasks.description: Set up the core logic in `.eleventy.js`, configure Tailwind's content paths, and establish global site data.
tasks.details:
1. Populate `src/_data/site.json`:
   ```json
   { "title": "My Personal Website", "url": "https://example.com", "authorName": "Your Name", "authorEmail": "you@example.com" }
   ```
2. Update `tailwind.config.js` to watch template files and add the typography plugin:
   ```javascript
   module.exports = {
     content: ["./src/**/*.{njk,md,html}"],
     theme: { extend: {} },
     plugins: [require('@tailwindcss/typography')],
   };
   ```
3. Populate `.eleventy.js` with plugins (RSS, SyntaxHighlight), passthrough copy for `/src/public/`, the `posts` collection (sorted by date descending), and utility filters (`readableDate`, `htmlDateString`). Add a `year` shortcode for the footer.
   ```javascript
   // In .eleventy.js
   // ... require statements ...
   eleventyConfig.addPlugin(pluginRss);
   eleventyConfig.addPlugin(syntaxHighlight);
   eleventyConfig.addPassthroughCopy('./src/public/');
   eleventyConfig.addCollection('posts', ...);
   eleventyConfig.addFilter('readableDate', ...);
   eleventyConfig.addShortcode('year', () => `${new Date().getFullYear()}`);
   ```

tasks.title: Implement Base Layout, Partials, and Global CSS
tasks.description: Create the main `base.njk` layout, header/footer partials, and the main CSS file with Tailwind directives.
tasks.details:
1. Create `src/assets/css/styles.css` with `@tailwind` directives.
2. Create `src/_includes/layouts/base.njk` with the core HTML structure, linking to `styles.css` and including header/footer partials.
3. Create `src/_includes/partials/header.njk` with site title and navigation (`Home`, `About`, `Blog`). Use `page.url` to highlight the active link.
4. Create `src/_includes/partials/footer.njk` with a copyright notice using the `{% year %}` shortcode.
<info added on 2025-06-24T11:28:13.636Z>
## Implementation Details

**Base Layout (`src/_includes/layouts/base.njk`)**:
- HTML5 document structure with proper meta tags for viewport and SEO
- Dynamic title handling: "Page Title | Site Title" format
- Meta description with fallback to site description
- Accessibility "Skip to main content" link
- Semantic HTML5 elements
- Script tag for main.js

**Header Partial (`src/_includes/partials/header.njk`)**:
- Modern design with shadow and border
- Site title linked to home page with hover effects
- Navigation menu with Home, About, Blog sections
- Active link highlighting with conditional blue color and bottom border
- Blog section highlights for both `/blog/` and post URLs
- Mobile-first responsive design with hamburger menu (visual only)
- Consistent hover and transition effects

**Footer Partial (`src/_includes/partials/footer.njk`)**:
- Centered copyright notice using `{% year %}` shortcode and `{{ site.author }}`
- Light gray background with proper spacing
- Responsive design matching header

**CSS Foundation**:
- Modern styling with consistent color scheme (gray and blue)
- Responsive breakpoints for mobile and desktop
- Accessibility features (focus states, skip links)
- Smooth hover transitions and active states
</info added on 2025-06-24T11:28:13.636Z>
tasks.testStrategy:
1. This task provides the visual foundation. To test, you must also complete Task 4 (Home Page).
2. After completing Task 4, run `npm start` and verify the basic page layout, header, and footer appear correctly on the home page.

tasks.title: Implement Static Pages: Home and About
tasks.description: Create the content for the Home and About pages.
tasks.details:
1. Create `src/index.njk` (Home page) with a welcome message. ```njk --- layout: layouts/base.njk title: Home ---

Welcome

...

``` 2. Create `src/about.njk` (About page) with bio content. Use the `prose` class from Tailwind Typography for styling. ```njk --- layout: layouts/base.njk title: About Me permalink: /about/index.html ---

About Me

...

```
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Run `npm start`. 
2. Navigate to `/` and `/about/`. Verify both pages render correctly with their content and the base layout.
3. Check that the `prose` styles are applied correctly on the About page.

tasks.title: Implement Blog Pages: Listing and Post Template
tasks.description: Create the blog listing page and the template for individual posts.
tasks.details:
1. Create `src/blog.njk` to list all posts from `collections.posts`. ```njk // Note: No '| reverse' filter needed as the collection is pre-sorted in .eleventy.js {% for post in collections.posts %}

{{ post.data.title }}

{{ post.date | readableDate }}

{% endfor %} ``` 2. Create the post layout `src/_includes/layouts/post.njk`. ```njk --- layout: layouts/base.njk ---

{{ title }}

{{ date | readableDate }}

{{ content | safe }}
``` 3. Add the CSS for the syntax highlighting plugin to `styles.css`. From the plugin's docs, this is typically a single line. ```css /* In styles.css */ @import 'prism-themes/themes/prism-one-dark.css'; /* Or your theme of choice */ ```
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Create a sample markdown post in `src/posts/` to test with.
2. Run `npm start` and navigate to `/blog/`. Verify the sample post is listed.
3. Click the link to the sample post. Verify it renders correctly using the `post.njk` layout and that any code blocks are syntax highlighted.

tasks.title: Finalize Blog Workflow and Documentation
tasks.description: Create a sample blog post demonstrating all features and document the creation process in the main README.
tasks.details:
1. Create a detailed sample post in `src/posts/my-first-post.md` using all required front matter (`title`, `date`, `layout`, `tags`, `permalink`). Include sample Markdown and a code block.
2. Update the root `README.md` with clear, concise instructions for future-you on how to create a new blog post, referencing the file structure and front matter requirements.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Follow the new instructions in `README.md` to create a *second* blog post.
2. Run `npm start` and verify this second post appears correctly on the blog index and on its own page.
3. This confirms the workflow is simple and the documentation is accurate.

tasks.title: Implement SEO and Accessibility Best Practices
tasks.description: Add a sitemap, robots.txt, RSS feed, and basic accessibility features.
tasks.details:
1. Create `src/public/robots.txt`.
2. Create a sitemap template `src/sitemap.xml.njk` that iterates through `collections.all`.
3. Create an RSS feed template `src/feed.xml.njk` using the helpers provided by `@11ty/eleventy-plugin-rss`.
4. Add the RSS feed link to the `<head>` of `src/_includes/layouts/base.njk`.
5. Add a "Skip to main content" link in `base.njk` for accessibility.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Run `npm run build`.
2. Verify `_site/sitemap.xml`, `_site/feed.xml`, and `_site/robots.txt` are generated correctly.
3. Validate the `feed.xml` using an online validator (e.g., W3C Feed Validation Service).
4. Use browser developer tools to run a Lighthouse audit and check for an accessibility score.

tasks.title: Setup Continuous Deployment with Netlify
tasks.description: Configure the project for automated deployment on Netlify.
tasks.details:
1. Ensure the `netlify.toml` file is configured correctly with the build command (`npm run build`) and publish directory (`_site`).
2. Create a new repository on your Git provider (GitHub, GitLab, etc.).
3. Push your local project to the remote repository.
4. In Netlify, create a 'New site from Git' and link it to your new repository.
5. Verify Netlify uses the settings from `netlify.toml` automatically.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. After connecting to Netlify, monitor the first deploy log for errors.
2. Access the live Netlify URL and verify the site is identical to the local build.
3. Make a small text change, commit, and push. Verify the site automatically redeploys with the change within a few minutes.
